## Data as code. {#data-as-code}
::: {.lede style="max-width: none;"}
**Data** is the content of each table: bytes in storage, each file named by its content.<br>
**Code** is everything about the data: which tables exist, which version is which,<br>where each came from, and the code that made it, all of which are small text files, tracked by git.
:::
::: {.sketch style="position: absolute; left: 150px; top: 330px; width: 1300px;"}
```{=html}
{{< include /sketches/split.svg >}}
```
:::
::: {.lede .fragment style="position: absolute; left: 0; right: 0; top: 735px; margin: 0 auto; text-align: center; max-width: none;"}
No database at work here: just a standardized way of storing each file, registering each file and storage, documenting each registry as code and then letting git do what it does best: tracking the code.
:::
::: notes
1:20 · 1 click

- Data: the values, in storage, named by content
- Code: everything about them, small text in git
- Why: data gets the collaboration open-source code already has
- Point at the glowing "the code" / "the data"
- Click: "We didn't build a database. We made the record code."
:::
